text:
maya: quick alert — p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~2.8s right after the autotune-scheduler rollout at 09:10 (canary -> global). Looks like the scheduler started grouping opposite-length requests into the same microbatch which blows up kv-cache miss and kernel path for short-seq flows. :eyes:

devin: on it. do we have a canary window id? also, is this only hosted or hitting dedicated too?

maya: canary id c-2026-09-22-0910, only hosted so far (global rollout set to 30% first). Dedicated metrics look stable.

raj: grabbing profiler traces for affected instances. initial flame shows heavy tail where GC-ish stalls + grpc queueing after kernel select. suspect the scheduler reordering caused longer dispatch delays for small requests.

olivia: throwing in recent p95/p99 numbers from observability: before: p95=210ms p99=420ms; after canary: p95=340ms p99=2.8s. request mix skewed to many short-seq chat completions so cost of wrong kernel select is amplified.

maya: here's the quick trace link (org dashboard): https://observ.redwood/trace/c-2026-09-22-0910 (sharing) — see stage "schedule->batch->kernel_select" where schedule latency jumps.

devin: can you paste the scheduler config change? I recall we switched heuristics to favor throughput by allowing heterogeneous microbatches to fill.

maya: config diff: 
```
- microbatch_policy: allow_mixed_lengths: false
+ microbatch_policy: allow_mixed_lengths: true
  microbatch_target_size: 2048
  autotune: enabled
```
The subtle change was flipping allow_mixed_lengths. That seems to have let very short and very long sequences mix.

raj: confirmed in flame: kv-cache hit-rate for short flows dropped ~35% during the window. Kernel selector then picked a slower kernel path (fallback) because the estimated seq distribution widened. That interaction caused per-request overhead and the long tail.

olivia: this is nasty because it's a throughput optimization that regresses tail. We should revert canary to 0% for now and roll back the change. Any objections?

devin: no objections. plan: 1) stop rollout (set canary to 0) 2) patch autotune to respect small-seq bias for latency-tier customers 3) re-run canary with synthetic short-seq load. I'll run the rollback now. :wrench:

infra-bot: deploybot: received rollback request for rollout c-2026-09-22-0910 by devin. Starting rollback to previous scheduler config (v1.9.3).

devin: running command: `redwoodctl rollout update --id c-2026-09-22-0910 --set canary=0`

infra-bot: deploybot: canary update applied. Traffic shifted back to baseline config across canary region (approx 2 minutes to fully converge).

maya: seeing p99 drop starting to recover — current window p95=230ms p99=470ms (within noise). Good catch.

raj: created a quick postmortem issue: https://issues.redwood/ENG-RT-527 - includes profiler dump, flame, and suggested fix: add a microbatch bias for seq-length < 64 and tighten autotune guardrails.

olivia: next steps: (1) patch autotune to include min-kv-warmup threshold (2) add an integration test simulating skewed short-seq workloads (3) change rollout policy to progressive ramp with latency SLO gating.

devin: agree. I'll bounce a candidate patch to the scheduler with the bias param disabled by default and a feature flag for experiments. Then run canary only after perf smoke tests.

maya: FYI adding "latency-gate" to rollout job (will fail the canary if p99 increases > 25% over baseline).

infra-bot: alerting: incident closed. Rollback confirmed by deploybot (rollback id r-2026-09-22-0912).

olivia: thanks everyone. small follow-up: Raj, can you attach the exact KV hit-rate graphs to ENG-RT-527? helps the platform team quantify severity.

raj: done — uploaded the graphs and the raw profiles. Also added a short note on kernel decision thresholds that flipped during mixed batches.

maya: closing thread. we should schedule a 15m debrief tomorrow to lock rollout gating rules. :calendar:
